VERDICT: FAIL as a strategy that beats SPY after tax with good confidence. It is a leverage bet whose vol targeting stops working in a CA taxable account.

- Reproduction: matches round 1 exactly. CA score +3.40, full +4.85, 10y beat 98%, 15y beat 100%, 20y beat 100% (only one 20-year window), boot p 0.011, max drawdown -61% vs SPY -55%. FED +3.64 / +6.32. NONE +4.01 / +3.40.
- Look-ahead: none. The rolling vol is read at today's bar. With a one-day lag: CA +3.34 / +6.18.
- Wash sales: 25% of realized-loss dollars were unenforced wash sales, because purchases in the 30 days before a loss sale are not checked and blocks use the combined result of a sale. The fix (`wash_pre`) gives CA +3.26 / +5.62, boot p 0.001. Not material.
- Negative cash after tax payments: immaterial (average -0.02% of portfolio value).
- DDM: legal as a different index, but the CA path holds 78% of the portfolio in DDM, so it is mostly a 2x Dow bet. DDM trailed SSO (14.2% vs 15.5% a year), so it was a drag; with SSO only, CA scores +4.58.
- Costs (CA score): 0 bps +3.62, 15 bps +3.11, 35 bps +2.24. In NONE at 35 bps: -1.41.
- Stricter tax accounting: -0.26 pp. Deflated Sharpe: 0.012 (CA).
- Main fragility: the 1% gain budget freezes exposure at about 1.9x from 2010 to 2026, including 2020 and 2022; in NONE those years average 1.31 and 1.14. Where it freezes depends on the path: at 15 bps it froze near 1.6x and ended with $1.16M instead of $2.03M. The full excess ranges +1.6 to +7.0 across lag, cost and wash-fix perturbations. COVID drawdowns for 2010-2016 starts were -52% to -58%, against SPY's -34%, the same as constant leverage.
- Vol targeting vs average leverage: constant 1.8 with the same execution scores CA +5.06 (full +3.59); SPY/SSO 18/82 bought once scores +5.03; 50/50 scores +3.39. In NONE, constant 1.65 scores +4.75 vs the candidate's +4.01, but with Sharpe 0.58 vs 0.70 and drawdown -77% vs -54%. Regression on SPY: CA beta 1.57, alpha -0.09%/yr (t = -0.04).
- Parameter grid (32 configs): the score rises with the target, i.e. leverage (15%: about -0.6 to 0; 30%: up to +4.8). The window barely matters.
- Long history (synthetic 2x with financing and fees, 1986-2026, CA): score +2.46, full +1.19, 10y beat 74%, 15y beat 72%, 20y beat 55%, boot p 0.26, max drawdown -79%, Sharpe 0.55 vs 0.67. Constant 1.8: full +2.49.
- 2000-2026 with synthetic SSO: score +3.11, full +1.72, boot p 0.25, max drawdown -68%.
- Pre-2000 holdout: +5.8 pp, but it sits inside a bull market and says little.

verdicts.candidate: TVT s21 t0.25 c2.0 v3 LSSO/DDM b0.1 gb0.01 (CA lead: tax-aware levered vol target)
reasons: The excess is beta, not skill. Monthly regression on SPY: CA beta 1.57, alpha -0.09%/yr (t = -0.04); NONE beta 1.29, alpha +0.69%/yr (t = 0.37). Deflated Sharpe at 12,000 trials: CA 0.012, FED 0.041, NONE 0.008.

In CA the vol targeting switches itself off. The 1% gain budget freezes exposure at 1.84-1.94x in every year 2011-2026, and at 1.8x or more on 85% of days (2020: 1.90, 2022: 1.89). In NONE the same years average 1.31 and 1.14. It de-levered only once, in 2008, while the lots were young.

The frozen level, and so the result, depends on the price path. At 15 bps costs exposure froze near 1.6x and ending equity was $1.16M instead of $2.03M. Full-period excess ranges +1.6 to +7.0 pp/yr across lag, cost and wash-fix perturbations.

Tail risk is understated. The -61% maximum drawdown of the 2006 start came in COVID 2020, not 2008. Starts in 2010-2016 lost 52-58% in COVID against SPY's 34%, the same as constant 1.8x. A 2008-sized crash after the freeze would cost about 80% (long history: -79%).

No value beyond average leverage. Constant 1.8 with the same execution scores CA +5.06 against +3.40; SPY/SSO 18/82 bought once +5.03; 50/50 bought once +3.39. In NONE, constant 1.65 (the candidate's average) scores +4.75 against +4.01. Vol targeting only lowers risk in tax-free accounts (Sharpe 0.70 vs 0.58).
Parameter grid (32 configs): the score rises with the target, i.e. leverage (15% target: -0.6 to +0.04; 30%: +2.6 to +4.8). The vol window barely matters (+3.2 to +3.9).

Long history with synthetic 2x S&P (financing and fees included), 1986-2026 CA: 10y beat 74%, 15y beat 72%, 20y beat 55%, boot p 0.26, max drawdown -79%, Sharpe 0.55 vs VFINX 0.67. 2000-2026 with synthetic SSO: boot p 0.25. Fails bar items 2, 3 and 7; round 1 found a negative walk-forward (item 4).

What does hold: no look-ahead (lag 1 gives CA +3.34 / +6.18), the wash-sale fix (+3.26 / +5.62), stricter tax accounting (-0.26 pp) and costs up to 15 bps (+3.11). The SSO-era excess is real as a leverage premium; it is not a confident SPY-beater.
bugs_found: Wash sales half enforced. TaxVT only blocks re-buying for 31 days after a sale whose combined result was a loss. It never checks purchases in the 30 days before a loss sale. On the 2006 CA path, 84 of 140 loss lots (25% of realized-loss dollars) are unenforced wash sales. The fix in verify_levvt.taxvt (wash_pre=true) leaves 0.4%. Impact: CA score +3.40 -> +3.26, full +4.85 -> +5.62. Not material.

Not a code bug, but a design flaw: with gain_budget=0.01, embedded gains freeze exposure after the first years, so the strategy is 'ratchet up to about 1.6-1.9x and hold'. The frozen level depends on the path, which makes single-path results fragile.

DDM is legal as a substitute (Dow vs S&P 500), but its lot logic sends most of the levered sleeve there: 78% of the portfolio on the CA path. The result is then partly a Dow-vs-S&P bet. DDM trailed SSO by 1.3%/yr over 2006-2026, a drag, not a flatter: SSO-only scores CA +4.58.
Minor: after the January tax payment, cash can sit below zero up to the 0.5% trigger (an unfunded balance). Average -0.02% of portfolio value, minimum -0.31%. Immaterial.
Lab note: verify_candidates.json stores 'cap': 2 and lever k as integers, so its JSON misses the round-1 cache entries keyed with 2.0. The results are identical.

summary: Verified risk_alloc.taxvt (target 25%, window 21, cap 2x, SPY/IWB/VTI with SSO/DDM, 1% gain budget). Verdict: FAIL as a confident SPY-beater. The SSO-era numbers reproduce exactly (CA score +3.40, full +4.85, boot p 0.011) and hold up under a one-day lag, a wash-sale fix (25% of realized losses were unenforced wash sales; fixed score +3.26), stricter tax accounting and costs up to 15 bps. But the excess is beta: 1.57 with zero alpha. In CA the gain budget freezes exposure at about 1.9x after 2009, so the vol targeting does nothing after its first years. The frozen level depends on the price path (full excess +1.6 to +7.0 under benign perturbations). After the freeze, drawdowns match constant leverage (COVID -52% to -58% vs SPY -34%). Constant leverage with the same average exposure, or a once-bought SPY/SSO mix, scores as well or better (+5.0). The parameter grid shows the score is set by the leverage level. The long history (synthetic 2x with financing) fails the bar: 10y beat 74%, 15y beat 72%, boot p 0.26, max drawdown -79%, Sharpe 0.55 vs 0.67. Deflated Sharpe is 0.01. open_questions: Should the lead present levered S&P exposure separately as an explicit risk-for-return choice (for example a once-bought SPY/SSO mix at 1.5x), rather than as a strategy that beats SPY? It has the same expected excess with about -70% to -80% drawdown risk.

The long-history test covers only 1986-2026, a strong period for US stocks. Leverage would likely look worse in 1966-1982 (high financing rates, flat real returns), but no total-return daily data was available to test it.
S&P 500 vs Russell 1000 (SPY/IWB) as wash-sale substitutes is an untested legal interpretation (about 0.99 correlation). A conservative investor might use only SPY/VTI.

A gain budget scaled to the size of the de-risking needed (or no budget during volatility spikes) might keep the vol targeting alive in taxable accounts. Not tested, because it would add degrees of freedom to a search that is already 12,000 configs deep.
